reasoning_input.question_text: Solve the first-order differential equation dy/dx + 2y = e⁻ˣ given that y = 2 when x = 0.

student_steps.content: Standard linear form: dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) with P(x) = 2 and Q(x) = e⁻ˣ
Integrating factor I(x) = e^(∫ 2 dx) = e^(2x)
Multiply equation by I(x): e^(2x) dy/dx + 2 e^(2x) y = e^(2x) e⁻ˣ = eˣ
Integrate both sides: y e^(2x) = ∫ eˣ dx = eˣ + C
Substitute x = 0, y = 2: 2 e⁰ = e⁰ + C → 2 = 1 + C → C = 1
y e^(2x) = eˣ + 1 → y = e⁻ˣ + e⁻²ˣ

steps.description: Identify P(x) = 2 and calculate integrating factor I(x) = e^(2x)
Multiply ODE by e^(2x) and rewrite LHS as d/dx [y e^(2x)]
Integrate RHS to obtain y e^(2x) = eˣ + C
Substitute initial condition (0, 2) to solve C = 1
State explicit general solution y = e⁻ˣ + e⁻²ˣ
